rationale: OCI-artifact packaging gives each model version a content-addressed, verifiable identity, letting an auditor confirm the model version used matches what's deployed.
Maintains a versioned model store so the exact model version used in an evaluation or audit can be retrieved and compared against the deployed one.
Cryptographic model signatures let an auditor verify the exact model version being evaluated matches the signed artifact that was deployed.
A verifiable signature over a model's weights is a concrete mechanism for demonstrating and verifying model ownership, the question RQ 57 asks about.
Generates auditor-traceable ML-BOM evidence at runtime, directly supporting verification that the model version audited matches what's actually running.
Diffing two AI-BOMs detects exactly when a model/component version has drifted, the core mechanism needed to verify an audited model version still matches production.
Automated discovery of deployed models/agents/APIs gives auditors ground truth to check the audited model version against, rather than relying on self-reported inventories.
Static-analysis-derived AI-component inventory helps confirm which model/version an application actually ships with, supporting audit-version verification.
